# Appeal of Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**Taylor Foster**
Member ID: W492196775
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-24 — Reference number POC-C65CA65DA3-33163**
**Member:** Taylor Foster | **Member ID:** W492196775
**Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Wyoming
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0736 — Hip Preservation Surgery (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0736.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), issued on 2026-08-24 under reference number POC-C65CA65DA3-33163. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the records in my file appear to meet the conservative care requirement written in Aetna's own policy, Aetna CPB 0736 — Hip Preservation Surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have set the plan's published language next to what is in my medical records.

## 1. The conservative treatment requirement — the reason given for the denial

The plan's policy states:

> "Failure to respond to all available conservative treatment options including: activity modification (e.g., restriction of athletic pursuits and avoidance of symptomatic motion), pharmacological intervention (e.g., non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS]), injections of local anesthetics into the joint) and physiotherapy."

And it sets the length of that treatment:

> "The treatment should be for at least 12 weeks in the past year with at least 6 weeks being formal physiotherapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist not virtual)."

My records establish each of these:

- **Physiotherapy:** supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, together with activity modification, from 2026-04-27 to 2026-08-03 — 14 weeks, with 18 visits completed. This exceeds both the 12-week total and the 6-week formal physiotherapy figure stated in the policy, and it falls within the past year.
- **Activity modification:** documented as part of that same course of therapy.
- **Pharmacological intervention:** NSAIDs for 8 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-14, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Failure to respond:** after all of the above, I continue to have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and I cannot run or squat.

## 2. How the physical therapy is documented

The plan's policy states:

> "Physical therapy (PT) needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history; and"

My physical therapy course is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. If that note was not included in the packet Aetna reviewed, I ask that this appeal be held open long enough for it to be supplied, and I request that Aetna also check my claims history for the 18 visits between 2026-04-27 and 2026-08-03.

## 3. The remaining criteria in the same policy

Although conservative care is the only reason given in the notice, the same policy section lists other requirements, and my records speak to them as well.

The plan's policy states:

> "Diagnosis of definite femoro-acetabular impingement (FAI) defined by appropriate imaging studies (X-rays, MRI or CT scans), showing labral pathology (e.g. partial or full thickness labral tearing or labral damage) with one or more of the following:"

and among the listed findings:

> "cam impingement (alpha angle greater than 50 degrees)"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip on 2026-07-11 reports an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees — above the 50-degree figure in the policy. The policy also states:

> "For purposes of this policy, Aetna will consider the official written report of complex imaging studies (e.g., CT, MRI, myelogram). If the operating surgeon disagrees with the official written report, the surgeon should document that disagreement."

The findings above are taken from the official written MRI arthrogram report.

The plan's policy states:

> "Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI (hip or groin pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities, with duration of at least 6 months where diagnosis of FAI has been made as above; and"

My records document 24 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest, sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and inability to run or squat. That is well beyond the 6-month figure in the policy, and it is pain brought on by exactly the flexion activities the policy describes.

The plan's policy states:

> "Absence of advanced osteoarthritis change on pre-operative X-ray (Tonnis grade 2 or more) or severe cartilage injury (Outerbridge grade III or IV); and"

and:

> "Absence of joint space narrowing on plain radiograph of the pelvis. Joint space is not less than 2 mm wide anywhere along the sourcil; and"

My imaging of 2026-07-11 reports joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0.

The plan's policy also states:

> "Positive impingement sign with sudden pain on 90 degree hip flexion with adduction and internal rotation or extension and external rotation; and"

My examination is documented as positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. If Aetna requires the specific maneuver and finding named in the policy to be spelled out, my surgeon can provide that detail from the examination record: [surgeon to specify provocative maneuver performed and result].

Finally, the policy states:

> "Member does not have generalized joint laxity especially in diseases connected with hypermobility of the joints, such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome; and"

> "Member does not have osteogenesis imperfecta; and"

> "All other potential sources of hip pain have been ruled out."

[Treating provider to confirm from the chart: absence of generalized joint laxity or hypermobility disorder; absence of osteogenesis imperfecta; and the workup ruling out other sources of hip pain.]

I would also note that one of the criteria above introduces a further list of conditions with a colon, and I have not been provided with the full text of every requirement in this policy. If Aetna applied a criterion that is not addressed in this letter, I ask that the plan identify in writing exactly which criterion it found unmet and what documentation would satisfy it.

## What I am asking for

I ask Aetna to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-24 (reference POC-C65CA65DA3-33163) and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914; or
2. If the denial is upheld in any part, tell me in writing which specific criterion of Aetna CPB 0736 — Hip Preservation Surgery was not met, what document would satisfy it, and the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the decision.

I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter (fax 859-425-3379). My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice — by **2027-02-20** — and this appeal is being submitted within that period.

Please contact me at [phone] or [email] if anything further is needed. I am happy to have my surgeon's office and my physical therapist send records directly.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Foster**
Member ID: W492196775
Date of birth: [DOB]
Reference number: POC-C65CA65DA3-33163

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-24
- MRI arthrogram report, 2026-07-11

- Office notes from Dr. Okafor, MD
- Record of corticosteroid injection, 2026-06-14
